newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Second Russia beet root test weight 85 grams.
newsitem.headline: Second Russia beet root test weight 85 grams.

text.p: Russia's second sugar beet test showed a root weight of 85 grams, compared with 76 grams at this time last year, the Semsvyokla sugar beet seed producers' association said on Wednesday.
Sugar content levels were not tested, but the association provided the following data for the test, which was conducted by Rossakhsvyokla, the sugar beet producers' association:
Semsvyokla said the next test would be conducted July 20 and would include data on sugar content. Daily root growth from the second test was 5.10 grams, up from 4.69 grams at this time last year.

NOTE - Russia began its sugar beet test cycle about 10 days earlier this year than in 1996. Rossakhsvyokla begins testing for sugar content levels only after conducting two tests for weight and planting density. Rossakhsvyokla data released from the 1996 cycle of tests began with the first test for sugar content, which was Russia's third test overall. All comparisons for 1997 data are for year-ago levels, and are not against the numerical number of the 1996 test.
